name: Gargoyle, Burning
body:
BURNING GARGOYLE
CR 4

XP 1,200
CE Medium monstrous humanoid (earth)

Init +6; Senses darkvision 60 ft.; Perception +5

DEFENSE

AC 16, touch 12, flat-footed 14 (+2 Dex, +4 natural)
hp 41 (5d10+15)
Fort +4, Ref +6, Will +4
DR 5/magic fire resistance 10

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft., fly 60 ft. (average)
Melee 2 claws +7 (1d6+2+1d6 fire) 1 bite +7 (1d4+2+1d6 fire)

STATISTICS

Str 15, Dex 14, Con 16, Int 6, Wis 11, Cha 7
Base Atk +5; CMB +7, CMD 19
Feats Hover, Improved Initiative, Skill Focus (Fly)
Skills Fly +12, Perception +5, Stealth +11 (+17 in stony areas); Racial Modifiers +2 Stealth (+6 in stony areas)
Languages Common, Terran, Ignan
SQ freeze

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Freeze (Ex)

A gargoyle can hold itself so still it appears to be a statue. A gargoyle that uses freeze can take 20 on its stealth check to hide in plain sight as a stone statue.

Flammable Secretions (Ex)

A Burning Gargoyle’s skin is fire resistant, and in addition it oozes out a sticky and highly flammable liquid from its pores. The liquid can be ignited as a swift action by a click of its fingers, causing the Burning Gargoyle to burn for a number of rounds equal to its Con score.

While ignited the Burning Gargoyle deals an extra 1d6 points of fire damage on each of its natural attacks. Anyone grappling the Burning Gargoyle or striking it with an unarmed attack will take 1d6 points of fire damage.

If the Burning Gargoyle is doused in water or the secretions are otherwise removed then the fires will be extinguished. Once the flame goes out the Gargoyle cannot use this ability again for 24 hours as the secretion is replaced.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary, pair or wing (3-12)
Treasure standard

These rarer cousins of the normal gargoyles are very similar to their more common kin. They share many of the same traits and abilities but they lack the vicious horns that would allow a gore attack and their skin is not so resistant to blows.

Instead they have gained the ability to secrete a flammable substance from their skin and set themselves on fire in a terrifying display as they swoop down on their prey.
